Q: How to achieve a 2 column grid of cards that expand into a full screen view when tapped upon? A:

The first problem that you described is an interesting one:

I tried using matchedGeometry as follows but that brings in the expanded view from the top left instead of expanding the card.

This is how the code you provided was working:

By default, .matchedGeometryEffect uses an anchor of .center, so I find it surprising that the views are not using the center of the screen as anchor for the transition.

To get it to work with the center of the screen as the anchor for the transition, it seems that the anchor for matchedGeometryEffect needs to be UnitPoint(x: 0.25, y: 0.25) instead. This represents a point half-way between the top-leading corner and the center. Other notes:

  • If you want to see the large view changing size as the animation is happening, use a frame with maxWidth and maxHeight, instead of a fixed width and height.
  • UIScreen.main.bounds is deprecated, so it is better not to use this. Also, it doesn't work with split screen on iPad.
  • In any case, it is not necessary to know the exact screen size, just use maxWidth: .infinity and maxHeight: .infinity instead.
  • The safe area insets complicate the anchor a bit. To keep the example simple, the code below does not ignore the safe area edges when the blue background is applied to the large view.
// CardView

VStack() {
    // ...
}
.frame(width: 150, height: 200)
.background(.blue)
.matchedGeometryEffect(id: "card", in: nameSpace, anchor: UnitPoint(x: 0.25, y: 0.25)) // 👈 anchor added

// ExpandedCardView

VStack {
    // ...
}
.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity) // 👈 updated
.background { Color.blue } // 👈 updated
.matchedGeometryEffect(id: "card", in: nameSpace, anchor: UnitPoint(x: 0.25, y: 0.25)) // 👈 anchor added

Here is how the example looks with these changes:

So changing the anchor for matchedGeometryEffect is a way to resolve the original issue of the drift in position that was happening during the transition.

Regarding your objective to achieve a 2 column grid of cards that expand into a full screen view when tapped:

  • My answer to Photos App-style .matchedGeometryEffect working unexpectedly shows how this can be done using matchedGeometryEffect (see part 2).

  • Another example can be seen in my answer to How to achieve animation similar to App store's feature view. This shows a different view in the expanded state, which is what you are doing too.

  • As an alternative mechanism, you could consider using navigationTransition and showing the selected note as a full screen cover. See my answer to How Do I Replicate the Exact Native iMessage Contact/Profile Transition Animation in iOS? for an example.

If you have difficulty getting the effect to work then I would suggest posting a new question that focuses on the specific issue you are having.

Q: Cleanly map DB constraint violations, no mimicking constraints in app A:

The root cause of this problem is using database for validation. If the team want to stick with this approach,

  • resolving message from ConstraintViolationException constraintName looks most pragmatic to me
  • if the constraintName is properly named with some rule or format, it is possible to handle dynamically, without updating the application.

However, implementing validation in application level is a more common approach.

  • proper input validation should be done before data being processed by business object and save to database
  • database constraint should be a guard for data integrity, and not for business rule checking. So we should consider those exception as server error when it happens. And should fix the missed application validation.

Q: How to bypass the 8-digit mark? A:

If you're using cmd then it's definitely not DOS. And "Command Prompt or Power Shell don't accept Long Filenames." is also completely wrong. All Windows tools support long file names

Q: Removing Specific Text from a String in powerapps A:

You don't need to store the result of the Substitute function in a variable - you can use it directly in the label within the gallery. For example, if the existing Text property in your label is set to

ThisItem.Value

You can update it to use the Substitute function, and you will have the result in that label directly:

Substitute(ThisItem.Value; "a"; "b")

Q: The following build commands failed A:

For me this was a caching issue causing the build to fail.

  1. Delete all DerivedData from your Library root folder

    rm -rf /Users/<Your Username>/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/*

    Obviously, replace <Your Username> with whatever your username is (if you're not sure, just run the $ whoami command)

  2. We need to clean cache

    • If you're using npm
    watchman watch-del-all; npm start -- --reset-cache;
    • If you're using yarn
    watchman watch-del-all; yarn start --reset-cache;

  3. Re-install pods

    cd ios; pod install; cd ..;

This worked for me at the very least.

Q: Does the combination of POSIX and C99 allow more negative values for ssize_t than -1? A:

While not guaranteed by the standard, most known implementations store ssize_t as a regular signed integer. A few VLIW architectures such as Itanium and Cerebras may map the NaT flag to the -1 value of ssize_t, though.
